type_name: Faulty Clock Rate Problem (Constant-Rate Clock Drift / Proportional Elapsed Time)
description: A clock gains time at a constant rate relative to an accurate one. Use the ratio of clock time to real time from a calibration interval to convert a later clock reading into actual time.

example.question: The clock in Sri's car, which is not accurate, gains time at a constant rate. One day as he begins shopping, he notes that his car clock and his watch (which is accurate) both say 12:00 noon. When he is done shopping, his watch says 12:30 and his car clock says 12:35. Later that day, Sri loses his watch. He looks at his car clock and it says 7:00. What is the actual time?
example.solution: Car clock shows 35 min per 30 real min. Elapsed car time 420 min -> 420 x 30/35 = 360 min = 6:00.
example.note: SAT_p1_15.html stores D (6:30) as the right answer, but the math gives 6:00 (B).

questions.question: The clock in Sri's car, which is not accurate, gains time at a constant rate. One day as Sri begins shopping, the car clock and Sri's watch (which is accurate) both say 12:00 noon. When done shopping, the watch says 12:30 and the car clock says 12:35. Later that day, Sri loses the watch. The car clock now says 7:00. What is the actual time?
questions.solution: The car clock runs 35 minutes for every 30 real minutes. Car clock elapsed = 420 min, so actual elapsed = 420 x 30/35 = 360 min after noon, so the actual time is 6:00.
